Since Zalacaine's inhibitory effect is on HTX-5D, not HTX-2C, there is no shared enzyme or mechanism between the two drugs in the information provided. Venafil's other properties (faecal excretion, half-life, food intake) do not suggest an interaction either. Therefore, no clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction is expected based on the available data.

MECHANISM: Zalacaine inhibits HTX-5D; Venafil is activated by HTX-2C — no overlapping pathway
